description: Component boundaries and dependency direction. Every rule here starts advisory: none has been run against real changes yet, and a rule that fires wrongly in its first week gets the whole system ignored. Promotion criteria say what would earn strictness.

rules.statement: Each component is declared in exactly one place: a directory annotation or the curated manifest, never both.
rules.rationale: Two declarations are two sources of truth for the same intent, which is the failure this system exists to prevent.
rules.promotion_criteria: No false positive across ten governed changes. This one is cheap to promote because the condition is unambiguous.

rules.statement: Every allowed or forbidden dependency names a declared component, and no component is both allowed and forbidden for the same dependent.
rules.rationale: A dependency rule naming a component that does not exist reads as protection while enforcing nothing.
rules.promotion_criteria: No false positive across ten governed changes.

rules.statement: Routes call services; they never import or call repositories directly.
rules.rationale: The service layer owns transaction boundaries and domain exceptions. A route reaching past it gets neither.
rules.promotion_criteria: The import graph exists and the rule runs clean on the current tree.

rules.statement: No component imports or calls a component listed in its forbidden_dependencies.
rules.rationale: Declaring a boundary and not enforcing it is worse than not declaring one, because it creates false confidence.
rules.promotion_criteria: The import graph exists; the rule runs clean; the declared boundaries have been reviewed against reality at least once.

rules.statement: Every REST call from the browser goes through a Next.js proxy route handler; the chat WebSocket is the only direct browser-to-backend edge.
rules.rationale: The proxy hop is part of every REST impact chain. Impact analysis that skips it reports the wrong blast radius, and a change that adds a second direct edge changes the security surface without looking like it does.
rules.promotion_criteria: The proxy mapping extractor lands and reproduces the reviewed baseline.

rules.statement: Long-running services declare a healthcheck, or reference an exception explaining why they do not.
rules.rationale: Compose dependency ordering is only meaningful when readiness is observable. A missing healthcheck turns depends_on into a guess.
rules.promotion_criteria: The Compose extractor lands and every current omission is either fixed or has an exception.

rules.statement: Routes, configuration variables, tools, and database tables have a consumer, or a classification explaining why they do not.
rules.rationale: Unused surface is either dead weight or an unfinished feature, and the two need opposite responses. Generator-provided but feature-disabled surfaces are neither, which is why the classification exists.
rules.promotion_criteria: Orphan detection runs with the generator-feature whitelist and produces no false positive on the current tree.

rules.statement: A thick service subpackage is imported only through its package root; sub-modules stay package-internal.
rules.rationale: The point of the subpackage boundary is that callers depend on the domain, not on how it is currently arranged inside.
rules.promotion_criteria: The import graph exists and the rule runs clean.
